questions.question: A solution is prepared by dissolving 0.005 moles of Ba(OH)$_2$ in 500 mL of water. Assuming complete dissociation, the pH of the solution is

options.explanation: Incorrect pH value
Incorrect pH value
Correct pH value, calculated from pOH = 1.7 and pH + pOH = 14
Incorrect pH value

questions.explanation: Ba(OH)$_2$ is a strong base and dissociates completely. Moles of Ba(OH)$_2$ = 0.005 mol. Volume of solution = 500 mL = 0.5 L. Concentration of Ba(OH)$_2$ = Moles / Volume = 0.005 mol / 0.5 L = 0.01 M. From the dissociation, [OH$^-$] = 2 × [Ba(OH)$_2$] = 2 × 0.01 M = 0.02 M. pOH = -log[OH$^-$] = -log(0.02) = -log(2 × 10$^{-2}$) = -(log 2 + log 10$^{-2}$) = -(0.3 - 2) = -(-1.7) = 1.7. pH + pOH = 14, pH = 14 - pOH = 14 - 1.7 = 12.3

questions.question: The pH of a 0.1 M NH₄Cl solution is 5.13. The pKb of NH₄OH is

options.explanation: Incorrect pKb value.
Correct pKb value.
Incorrect pKb value, this is the pH value.
Incorrect pKb value.

questions.explanation: NH₄⁺ is the conjugate acid of NH₄OH. pH = 5.13 → pOH = 14 – 5.13 = 8.87 → pKb = pOH – log C = 8.87 – log 0.1 = 8.87 – (–1) = 9.87. But since NH₄Cl gives acidic solution, the correct pKb of NH₄OH = 14 – pKa(NH₄⁺) = 14 – (14 – pKb) = pKb = 4.87.
